items.title: Willie Hightower Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: Zoo told me he wanted me to come over to the casino... So, I followed him the next night that I went down and went over to the casinos.

ctx.x: What color were the coats? Blue, you know like brass band they get, blue.

Blue, you know like a little bit, and white shoes. Well the shoes didn't cost but 75 cents a dollar in those days, see. That white, you can be shoes, see. And the first job that we went on was in Audubon Park. And when we went up there, they had a servant to come to the door and tell us, oh my God, go to the back, don't come in the front, go around the back. And they had us to come in the back. She said, oh you like the crap and everything. The madam said she don't like so and so. Black color people come to the…
He looks a little bit like, his pictures look like Peter Boccage almost.

ctx.x: Willie Hightower on trumpet, Elvin Zoo Roberson on trombone. Way left that band went to Oak, Oakland, California.
He played with Ory and Mud Carey and some of that. Yeah, that's right.
